svg.text: Helping a new team member find their voice
Joining a new team can leave someone ambivalent about speaking up, so a welcoming
When our newest colleague arrived, we asked how she was settling in instead of assuming she felt comfortable. She
seemed unsure about the next project, and a discerning question helped us understand her concern. We invited her
to flesh out an idea before trying to iron out the practical details.
At first, the room was quiet, so I tried to read the room rather than demand an immediate answer. A smaller
discussion might give everyone more confidence. When she said, “I could use a hand with this,” two colleagues
Patient questions and practical support can move the needle toward trust.
